- Brown/dried dead plant tissue
- Some possible white material on stems
- Healthy plants surrounding the affected area
- Early growth stage

Top candidates: Pythium_damping_off, Rhizoctonia, White_Mold, Phytophthora

Let me view reference images for these candidates.
The White Mold reference image (top-right panel) shows a very similar field scene to the test image - dead/collapsed plants amid green healthy ones. Let me look at a couple more candidates.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image key features:**
- Dense soybean canopy at mid-season stage
- Cluster of dead/collapsed plants in the center
- Bleached/white stem appearance on dead plants
- Dead leaves remaining attached while turning brown
- Pods visible on some plants
- Healthy plants surrounding the dead cluster

**Comparison with references:**
- **White Mold**: The top-right panel of the White Mold collage shows an almost identical scene — dead/collapsed plants amid a green canopy, with white bleached stems. The pattern of girdled stems causing plant collapse at nodes matches perfectly.
- **Phytophthora**: Shows more standing dead plants with brown stem discoloration from soil line — different pattern
- **Pythium**: Very early seedling stage only
- **Rhizoctonia**: Shows stem lesions, more individual plant damage

The collapsed cluster of dead plants with bleached/white stems and dead leaves remaining attached is characteristic of White Mold. The White Mold reference image shows nearly identical field appearance.
